title: Schizophrenia, schizoaffective and bipolar disorder
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's psychiatric condition.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for psychiatric management.

HPI
Pt is an 80-year-old female presenting for scheduled follow-up of schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type. Pt reports she has been feeling stable over the past month. Denies significant mood swings or sleep disturbances. Adherent to current medication regimen. No acute distress noted during interview.

Medication List
1. Quetiapine 100mg PO QHS
2. Lithium Carbonate 300mg PO BID
3. Multivitamin daily

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, weight change.
Psychiatric: Denies mood instability, sleep issues.
Neurological: Denies tremors, dizziness.
Other: Denies any acute complaints.

Social History
Pt lives at home with her daughter. Retired. No tobacco or recreational drug use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, stroke.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes.

Vitals
BP: 128/82
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
Lithium level: 0.8 mEq/L
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
HbA1c: 5.8%
eGFR: 65 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
General: Pt is alert and oriented x3. Cooperative.
Appearance: Well-groomed, appropriate dress.
Psych: Affect is full and congruent. Speech is clear and normal rate/volume. Thought process is linear and goal-directed. Insight and judgment are fair.
Physical: CTAB. Heart: RRR. Lungs: Clear to auscultation. Extremities: No edema.

Assessment
1. Schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type. Pt is currently stable on her antipsychotic and mood stabilizer.

Plan
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Continue monitoring lithium levels and renal function.
3. Follow up in 3 months for routine psychiatric evaluation.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 10/14/2026

distractors.why: Schizoaffective disorder is a separate category (F25).
'Bipolar type' describes the schizoaffective disorder; it is not bipolar disorder.
